rawFindings.title: Incorrect placeholder replacement using repeated '%' characters
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaces a global regular expression ('/%/g') with a string literal ('%') in mout.string.replace, which likely only replaces the first occurrence of '%' instead of all occurrences. This is a regression from the prior behavior, which replaced all '%' characters in the script string.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the use of a global regular expression for the replacement, i.e., use new RegExp('%', 'g') instead of the string '%'. Use mout.string.replace(config.scripts[action], /%/g, orderedPackages.join(' ')) to replace all placeholders correctly.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect use of RegExp for replacing placeholders in hook function
rawFindings.explanation: The code previously created a global RegExp to replace all '%' characters but the new code uses a string '%' which only replaces the first occurrence. This can cause the replacement to miss multiple '%' placeholders expected in the script commands.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert to using RegExp with global flag for replacement: var placeholder = new RegExp('%', 'g'); var cmdString = mout.string.replace(config.scripts[action], placeholder, orderedPackages.join(' '));

rawFindings.title: Test changes do not match change in placeholder replacement behavior
rawFindings.explanation: The tests were changed to expect filenames with only one packageName instead of two, but the actual code now replaces only one '%' placeholder. This change reduces the script's capability to handle multiple placeholders and may not match user expectations or existing scripts requiring multiple replacements.
rawFindings.suggestion: Either revert the test case changes to expect two placeholders or update the code to support multiple placeholders consistently.
